Yes, only Owner and Admin roles can access the API credentials page. Read-only and Editor roles receive 403 from the credentials endpoint. A read-only user cannot create API credentials, create reports, modify settings, invite users, or access the application token page at all. The API credentials page returns a 403 for Read-only accounts. To create an API credential, sign in as Owner or Admin, open Settings > API credentials, create key, copy the secret once, and then use the API credentials page to create a new API key. Editor/Read-only roles have no access to the API credentials page, and the API refuses their tokens (HTTP 403).
Follow-up: Is there any way to grant API-key access to lower roles? Yes, see User roles and permissions. The API rejects the request because the owner has the right to create, list, and revoke API credentials. There is no way to grant API-key access to lower roles. See User roles and permissions.
